stories.title: Trump Confirms Fort Hood Shooter's Execution Will Not Be Livestreamed
stories.summary: President Trump announced that the execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan by firing squad will not be livestreamed, reversing a previous statement from Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The decision follows bipartisan backlash against the Pentagon's initial plan to broadcast the execution. Families of the victims will have the option to attend the execution in person.

stories.title: Ukraine Resumes Strikes on Russian Oil Refineries Following Truce Breakdown
stories.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced that Ukraine will resume attacks on Russian oil refineries, declaring an end to a temporary ceasefire. This decision follows renewed Russian strikes on Ukrainian infrastructure. Reports indicate that Ukrainian drones targeted a refinery in Russia's Ryazan region shortly after Zelensky's announcement.

stories.title: Tragic School Roof Collapse in Pakistan Claims Lives of Children and Teacher
stories.summary: A roof collapse at a private school in Peshawar, Pakistan, has resulted in the deaths of at least 28 to 35 individuals, primarily children, along with one teacher. The incident occurred on October 15, 2026, and more than 50 others were reported injured. Local authorities have indicated that the roof was structurally weak and had been overloaded due to ongoing construction work. The school's owner has been arrested as investigations continue.

stories.summary: The New Yalu River Bridge, connecting Dandong in China and Sinuiju in North Korea, has officially opened after a 12-year delay. This four-lane road bridge is expected to enhance regional trade and cooperation between the two nations, which have been strengthening their ties recently.

stories.title: Scrutiny Grows Over Credentials of Trump's New Press Secretary Katie Zacharia
stories.summary: Katie Zacharia, the newly appointed White House press secretary, is facing increasing scrutiny regarding her legal credentials. Questions have arisen about her claims of being a lawyer, as reports indicate she may not be registered with the bar in any state where she has lived. Additionally, her first day in the role was marked by an unclear response about where she passed the bar exam.

stories.title: Juror in Lindsay Clancy Mistrial Claims Harassment and Discusses Evidence
stories.summary: Michael P. Desronvil, the only holdout juror in Lindsay Clancy's mistrial, reported feeling harassed since the trial concluded in September. Desronvil also noted that all jurors had phones during the trial, as the defense seeks records related to his communications.

Rama has stated he will not resign amid the ongoing unrest, which has also spread to other cities.
